payload.task_text:
Our company is launching a wellness program and I have been asked to coordinate the cafeteria lunch menu for the upcoming week. There is a corporate nutrition guidelines page available at http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html that outlines the daily nutritional intake targets for a healthy adult, including recommended calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate amounts per meal, along with notes about common dietary restrictions our employees have reported such as vegetarian and low-sodium preferences.

Please start by visiting that guidelines page and extracting all the nutritional targets and dietary notes listed there. The page has a table with per-meal targets for lunch specifically, and a section listing the top dietary restrictions reported by employees.

Next, search the recipe database for Chinese dishes that would be suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch. I need you to find at least two main dishes from the meat category, at least two dishes from the vegetable category, and at least one soup or staple dish. For each dish, note the name, category, and any available ingredient or preparation details.

Once you have the recipes, create a Google Sheets spreadsheet called "Wellness_Lunch_Menu" with a sheet named "Weekly_Plan". This sheet should have columns for Day (Monday through Friday), Main_Dish_1, Main_Dish_2, Side_Dish, Soup_Or_Staple, Estimated_Calories, Estimated_Protein_g, Estimated_Fat_g, and Estimated_Carbs_g. Assign the recipes you found across the five days, reusing dishes if needed but trying to vary the menu. Fill in estimated nutritional values per meal based on reasonable estimates for Chinese dishes, keeping them within the guidelines you found on the website. Add a second sheet called "Nutrition_Summary" with columns for Nutrient, Daily_Target, Menu_Average, and Within_Target (Yes or No), with rows for Calories, Protein, Fat, and Carbs.

After the spreadsheet is ready, write a Word document called Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx in the workspace. This document should have a title "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program", a brief introduction explaining the program goals, a section listing the five daily menus with dish names, and a section summarizing how the menu aligns with the nutritional guidelines. Mention any dishes that accommodate dietary restrictions.

Finally, send an email from wellness@company.com to cafeteria-manager@company.com with the subject "Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026" that provides an overview of the meal plan, highlights the nutritional targets from the guidelines, and lists all the dishes selected for the week.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, run the four independent read-only sources in one wave and keep their complete page/category responses out of the main context. The recipe categories can exceed the model-output limit, so their owners must be explore sub-agents constrained to read-only source work; they may read the runtime `output_path` but must not write a deliverable or mutate any external system.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 4 explore sub-agents as parallel individual Agent calls:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to read the complete nutrition-guidelines page at `http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html` with read-only browser operations. Return the exact lunch targets for calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates, every reported dietary restriction/note, and page/table/field controls.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `荤菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"荤菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   3. explore 2 (web-domain-researcher 2): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `素菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"素菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   4. explore 3 (web-domain-researcher 3): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact category `汤`; only when that returned collection has no usable recipe may it query exact category `主食`. Consume any overlong runtime `output_path` from the task workspace without repeating the call, select at least one suitable exact recipe ID, retrieve only that ID, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], requested_category:"汤", used_category, fallback_reason, category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.

After Wave 1, the main agent must require at least two meat, two vegetable, and one soup/staple recipe with unique exact IDs, freeze an explicit Monday-Friday menu (reusing only those verified dishes when needed), and derive reasonable meal-level estimates that remain consistent with the source targets. Freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`. From that frozen menu, dispatch the three independent output branches in the same response: (1) coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): own exactly one `Wellness_Lunch_Menu` spreadsheet with `Weekly_Plan` and `Nutrition_Summary` using the task's exact columns/rows; (2) coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): own `<agent_workspace>/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx` with the exact title, five daily menus, guideline alignment, and supported dietary accommodations; and (3) coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): send exactly one message from `wellness@company.com` to `cafeteria-manager@company.com` with subject `Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026`. Read both artifacts once in native-parallel calls, then reconcile dish names, targets, estimates, averages, Within_Target decisions, and email content. Do not dispatch a verification agent.

You are a read-only web researcher. Your ONLY job is to read a single webpage and report its contents verbatim. Do NOT write any files, do NOT modify anything, do NOT use write tools.

Task: Navigate to http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html using the read-only browser tools available to you (e.g. mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_navigate, then browser_snapshot, browser_snapshot_search, browser_snapshot_navigate_* to view all spans of the page). If the page has more content than fits in one snapshot, explore all spans until you have the complete content.

This page is a corporate nutrition guidelines page for a wellness program. It contains:
1. A table with per-meal nutritional targets for a healthy adult — especially for LUNCH: recommended calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate amounts per meal.
2. A section listing the top dietary restrictions reported by employees (e.g. vegetarian, low-sodium, allergies, etc.), along with any other notes.

Return a structured report containing:
- lunch_targets: {calories: <value with unit>, protein: <value with unit>, fat: <value with unit>, carbs: <value with unit>} — quote EXACT numbers/units as displayed
- any other per-meal targets shown (breakfast, dinner, etc. if present)
- dietary_restrictions: complete list of every dietary restriction/note reported by employees, quoted exactly
- additional_notes: any other relevant notes from the page
- page_controls: any interactive elements (buttons, tabs, links, table headers) visible on the page
- source_url: the URL you read

Be exhaustive and exact — this data will be used as the ground truth for a nutrition-focused deliverable. Include every number and note verbatim.
Read nutrition guidelines page

You are a strictly read-only exploration sub-agent for a Chinese recipe database. Do NOT write any deliverable files, do NOT modify or create any recipe, do NOT mutate any external system. You may only read.

Context: We are building a corporate cafeteria lunch menu. We need main dishes from the meat category.

Step 1: Call the recipe database tool mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory with category="荤菜" (meat dishes). 
IMPORTANT: If the response to this call is materialized as an overlong runtime file path (an "output_path" pointing into the task workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace or similar), DO NOT retry the category call. Instead read that output file from the task workspace (you have read access to the workspace) to get the full category listing.

Step 2: From the returned category listing, select at least TWO distinct recipe IDs that are suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch (reasonable portion, common dish, no exotic/unavailable ingredients). Prefer complete, well-known dishes.

Step 3: Retrieve ONLY the selected recipe IDs using native parallel calls to mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById for each selected ID (the query parameter accepts the recipe name or ID).

Step 4: Return a structured report:
- recipes: [{recipe_id, name, category, ingredients, preparation}] for each selected recipe — include the FULL ingredient list and preparation/steps as returned
- category: "荤菜"
- category_result_count: how many recipes the category contains
- selected_count: how many you selected
- duplicate_ids: any duplicate recipe IDs you noticed
- missing_fields: any selected recipe missing name/category/ingredients/preparation data

Be accurate and complete — the recipe details you return will be used verbatim to build a menu document and spreadsheet.
Query 荤菜 category recipes

You are a strictly read-only exploration sub-agent for a Chinese recipe database. Do NOT write any deliverable files, do NOT modify or create any recipe, do NOT mutate any external system. You may only read.

Context: We are building a corporate cafeteria lunch menu. We need one soup or staple dish. The primary category is "汤" (soup); only if that category yields no usable recipe may you fall back to category "主食" (staple foods).

Step 1: Call the recipe database tool mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory with category="汤" (soup).

You are an external-workflow operator. Your ONLY deliverable: create ONE Google Sheets spreadsheet named "Wellness_Lunch_Menu" containing exactly two sheets, "Weekly_Plan" and "Nutrition_Summary", with the exact content below. Use the mcp__google_sheet__* tools. Do not create any other files or send any emails.

FROZEN DATA (do not invent or alter values):

Weekly_Plan sheet — headers and 5 data rows (Day = Monday..Friday; dish names in Chinese with English gloss):

Headers: Day | Main_Dish_1 | Main_Dish_2 | Side_Dish | Soup_Or_Staple | Estimated_Calories | Estimated_Protein_g | Estimated_Fat_g | Estimated_Carbs_g

Row1: Monday | 可乐鸡翅 (Cola Chicken Wings) | 地三鲜 (Di San Xian) | 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds) | 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 670 | 32 | 24 | 66
Row2: Tuesday | 糖醋里脊 (Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin) | 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds) | 西红柿炒鸡蛋 (Tomato & Egg Stir-fry) | 白米饭 (Steamed Rice) | 745 | 36 | 25.5 | 82
Row3: Wednesday | 乡村啤酒鸭 (Country Beer Duck) | 地三鲜 (Di San Xian) | 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds) | 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 690 | 35 | 26 | 57
Row4: Thursday | 可乐鸡翅 (Cola Chicken Wings) | 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds) | 西红柿炒鸡蛋 (Tomato & Egg Stir-fry) | 白米饭 (Steamed Rice) | 735 | 37 | 25.5 | 76
Row5: Friday | 糖醋里脊 (Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin) | 地三鲜 (Di San Xian) | 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds) | 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 680 | 31 | 24 | 72

Nutrition_Summary sheet — headers and 4 data rows:
Headers: Nutrient | Daily_Target | Menu_Average | Within_Target
Calories | 650 | 704 | Yes
Protein | 30 | 34.2 | Yes
Fat | 22 | 25 | Yes
Carbs | 80 | 70.6 | Yes

EXECUTION STEPS:
1. Call mcp__google_sheet__create_spreadsheet with title "Wellness_Lunch_Menu". Note the returned spreadsheet_id.
2. The new spreadsheet contains a default sheet (likely "Sheet1"). Rename it to "Weekly_Plan" (mcp__google_sheet__rename_sheet). If instead the tool created a sheet named differently, list sheets (mcp__google_sheet__list_sheets) and rename the default tab to "Weekly_Plan".
3. Create a second sheet titled "Nutrition_Summary" (mcp__google_sheet__create_sheet).
4. Fill Weekly_Plan: write the header row at A1:I1 and the 5 data rows at A2:I6 (use mcp__google_sheet__update_cells with sheet "Weekly_Plan", range "A1:I6"). Numbers must be written as numbers (670, 32, 24, 66, 745, 36, 25.5, 82, 690, 35, 26, 57, 735, 37, 25.5, 76, 680, 31, 24, 72).
5. Fill Nutrition_Summary: write headers at A1:D1 and 4 data rows at A2:D5 (values 650, 704, Yes / 30, 34.2, Yes / 22, 25, Yes / 80, 70.6, Yes).
6. Verify by reading both sheets back (mcp__google_sheet__get_sheet_data for each) and confirm all rows/columns are correct.

RETURN a report with: the spreadsheet_id, the spreadsheet title, list of sheet names, and a confirmation that Weekly_Plan has 9 columns x 6 rows and Nutrition_Summary has 4 columns x 5 rows with values matching the frozen data above (paste back the read data).
Create Wellness_Lunch_Menu spreadsheet

You are an office-report builder. Your ONLY deliverable: create a Word document at the exact absolute path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx
Use the mcp__word__* tools. Do not create spreadsheets or send emails.

CONTENT TO INCLUDE (use the exact title and structure):

1. Document title (Heading level 1): "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program"

2. Introduction (a few paragraphs): Our corporate wellness program runs March 10-14, 2026 (Monday through Friday) with a Chinese Cuisine theme. The goal is to offer balanced, nutritious cafeteria lunches that meet the corporate nutrition guidelines established with registered dietitians: per lunch meal, 500-800 kcal (target 650), 20-45 g protein (target 30), 15-30 g fat (target 22), and 55-110 g carbohydrates (target 80), all per single serving. The menu also aims to accommodate employee dietary restrictions reported in the Q4 2025 survey (847 respondents): vegetarian (23%), low-sodium (18%), no-pork (15%), and gluten-free (12%).

3. Section "Five Daily Menus" (Heading 2) listing each day with its dishes:
- Monday: 可乐鸡翅 (Cola Chicken Wings), 地三鲜 (Di San Xian), 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds), 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)
- Tuesday: 糖醋里脊 (Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin - CONTAINS PORK, clearly labeled), 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds), 西红柿炒鸡蛋 (Tomato & Egg Stir-fry), 白米饭 (Steamed Rice)
- Wednesday: 乡村啤酒鸭 (Country Beer Duck), 地三鲜 (Di San Xian), 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds), 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)
- Thursday: 可乐鸡翅 (Cola Chicken Wings), 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds), 西红柿炒鸡蛋 (Tomato & Egg Stir-fry), 白米饭 (Steamed Rice)
- Friday: 糖醋里脊 (Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin - CONTAINS PORK, clearly labeled), 地三鲜 (Di San Xian), 酸辣土豆丝 (Hot & Sour Potato Shreds), 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)

4. Section "Nutritional Guidelines Alignment" (Heading 2): explain that every daily menu falls within the guideline ranges (Calories 500-800, Protein 20-45 g, Fat 15-30 g, Carbs 55-110 g per lunch). Include the weekly averages: 704 kcal, 34.2 g protein, 25 g fat, 70.6 g carbohydrates — all within the acceptable ranges. Note each meal includes at least one dish with 15g+ protein (the meat main dish), at least one vegetable dish, and a soup or staple.

5. Section "Dietary Accommodations" (Heading 2): mention that a fully vegetarian main option (e.g., 地三鲜, 酸辣土豆丝, 西红柿炒鸡蛋) is offered every day; low-sodium preparation (reduced soy sauce/salt) is applied, e.g., 酸辣土豆丝 and 紫菜蛋花汤; gluten-free-friendly options such as 西红柿炒鸡蛋 and 紫菜蛋花汤 are available; and pork-containing dishes (糖醋里脊) are clearly labeled for the no-pork employees.

EXECUTION STEPS:
1. mcp__word__create_document with filename = the absolute path above (title "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program" optional).
2. Add the Heading 1 title, then paragraphs/sections using mcp__word__add_heading (level 1 for the title, level 2 for section headers) and mcp__word__add_paragraph for body text. Use the content above.
3. Verify: call mcp__word__get_document_text on the created file and paste the extracted text back in your final report to confirm the title, five menus, alignment section, and accommodations are all present.

RETURN a report with the absolute file path, confirmation the file exists, and the extracted document text.
Create Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx
